current_boundary.routine_semantics: At stage+0x9f93 the helper loads its length argument, at +0x9f99 it loads the mapping base, and at +0x9f9f it decrements length before a byte-zeroing loop. The zero synthetic length therefore becomes 0xffffffff and the first store targets base-1.
current_boundary.conclusion: The zero-filled synthetic mshtml view leaves the zero-fill helper with a zero length, which underflows to mapping base minus one. The verified handler rejects access addresses above 0x10000, so this is a hard evidence boundary rather than another exception-obfuscation skip. Real mshtml image bytes and layout are required to recover the intended nonzero range and continue faithfully.

assumptions_and_limits: The child ntdll slot, old export pointer, module returns, TEB/PEB structures, 12 windows, successful thread-hide call, debug-port zero and large sparse allocation remain synthetic.
The mshtml mapping is a zero-filled 0x20000 fixture inherited from the parent mapping assumption. It contains no Windows DLL bytes.
The no-marker control preserves the real setup and terminal iteration while omitting middle page-scan iterations.
The model executes x86 instructions only. It does not reproduce a real scheduler race between NtResumeThread and the pointer overwrite.
No final payload, family attribution or endpoint is claimed. Sparse companion-file relationships and the production NSIS instruction-stream extraction gap remain unresolved.
